title: attn-hyperbridge-fused-qkv-concat-rope-prefetch-optimizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce the HyperBridge fused attention kernel with adaptive prefetching and KV warmup. Improves median latency and throughput for long-context workloads and provides a safe rollout path via config flags.
description: Motivation: Long-context generation workloads show large variance in latency due to non-ideal prefetching, KV cache cold starts, and per-request kernel dispatch overhead. This PR introduces the HyperBridge attention kernel, an opt-in FlashAttention-derived variant that fuses Q/K/V concat, applies rotary/rope-aware remapping, and cooperates with a small adaptive prefetch scheduler to keep the KV working set warm under continuous batching. Key changes: 1) new kernel implementation in native runtime that concatenates Q/K/V during initial load to reduce memory traffic, 2) rotary/rope index remapping to avoid repeated strided loads for rotary embeddings, 3) an adaptive prefetch scheduler that monitors sequence length and KV hit rates to trigger background warmup with low-priority tokens, 4) hooks into continuous-batching to group warmup traffic and preserve latency SLOs, and 5) configuration flags and heuristics to fall back to stock FlashAttention when hardware or model shape is incompatible. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on A100-40GB and T4 show P50 latency reductions of 8-14% and sustained throughput improvements of 12-20% on long-context (8k+) workloads with 8-24 batch sizes. End-to-end customer traces using a conversational reranker show token cost down 9% and tail latency improvements for cold-start sessions. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.feature.hyperbridge in config, gradual canary on Dedicated for 2 weeks with automatic rollback on perf regressions, and step increase to Hosted after linear ticket ENG-4218 verification. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. The kernel is disabled by default for Hosted until canary completes. Checklist: [x] kernel implementation [x] scheduler integration [x] KV warmup metrics [x] unit and integration tests [x] perf harness results attached [x] docs and rollout notes. Related: internal doc at https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-4218 and experiment board ENG-4301.

Lucía Gómez: Benchmarks look promising. Please include a comparison with the existing lazy-KV warmup on T4 to ensure no regression on smaller GPUs.
Maya Chen (author): Added T4 numbers to the perf harness and included results in benchmarks/hyperbridge/README.md. T4 shows 8-12% throughput gains for long contexts.
